items.requirement: The service must support multiple customer companies on a shared platform while keeping each company's drones, sites, and charging pads separate from other companies so that charging pads are never lent or assigned to another company.

The service must allow a fleet technician to add new drones to a company's fleet and retire old ones, recording each drone's home site, manufacturer, model, carrying capacity, full-battery flight range, sensors, and charging connector type.
The service must support managing up to a few hundred drones and a few dozen charging pads per company.
The service must allow a fleet technician to set up and manage charging pads at a company's sites, recording the specific non-interchangeable charging connector type each pad supports.

The service must allow a fleet technician to send a drone to charge at one of its company's charging pads, and must not assign a drone to a charging pad whose connector type does not match the drone's connector type.

The service must allow a fleet technician to take a drone out of service for repairs and put it back in service afterwards, and must prevent an out-of-service drone from being assigned to or signed off for a flight.
The service must record repairs and servicing carried out on each drone so a company can show regulators how its drones have been looked after.

The service must handle reports from drones that arrive late, out of order, more than once, or not at all—such as in patchy radio coverage around ports, industrial sites, or bad weather—without corrupting state or duplicating recorded events.

The service must handle unreliable instruction links to drones and charging equipment so that retrying an instruction when delivery of the first attempt is uncertain does not cause unintended duplicate execution if the instruction arrives twice.
The service must account for faster battery drain in cold and wind than planned rather than assuming nominal full-battery range always applies when planning flights or sending drones to charge.

The service must allow a licensed dispatcher to plan a flight by selecting which drone flies along which route of flight corridors between sites, displaying the available drones' carrying capacity, range, sensors, and operational status.
The service must require a licensed dispatcher to sign off on a flight before it leaves, and must not allow an unlicensed user to sign off on a flight.
The service must prevent conflicting assignments when multiple dispatchers plan flights at the same time for the same busy sites or popular drones.
The service must allow a dispatcher to call off a flight.
The service must track and reflect events occurring outside the dispatcher's control, including whether loads are ready or not, and drones reaching their points and arriving.

The service must allow the platform's airspace desk to maintain a shared picture of the airspace across customers, consisting of the network of flight corridors between sites and the zones that group them.

The service must allow the airspace desk to enter and update airspace closures announced by authorities and reflect those closures in the shared airspace picture used for planning and running flights.
When an airspace closure is entered, the service must calculate and show the airspace desk how much disruption the closure caused across customers.
